history.rationale: Corresponds to the canonical Henipavirus V507I m102.4 escape mutation, introducing steric bulk that impairs Fab packing while preserving ephrin binding.
Modifies key contact residue D555 by eliminating negative charge, disrupting m102.4 electrostatic interactions with minimal receptor disruption.
Targets critical contact residue E533 with a charge reversal that strongly repels m102.4 CDR paratope loops outside the core ephrin pocket.
Neutralizes acidic charge at E533, attenuating hydrogen bonding and electrostatic complementarity to m102.4 without destabilizing the head domain.
Provides a subtle steric extension at position D555 that disrupts precise paratope fitting for m102.4 while retaining ephrin-B2/B3 compatibility.
Removes the functional carboxylate sidechain at D555, abolishing specific contacts necessary for high-affinity m102.4 neutralization.
Truncates the hydrophobic sidechain at V507, weakening nonpolar packing against m102.4 CDRs while maintaining fold stability.
Introduces an acidic sidechain at N557 on the epitope periphery to disrupt local electrostatic complementarity to m102.4.
Removes polar interactions at position Q530, a recognized m102.4 contact residue that tolerates mutation without loss of receptor binding.
Places a positively charged lysine at E554 to destabilize the m102.4 interface through repulsive electrostatic interactions.
